title: Power Automate: Delinea Secret Server as a credential provider for desktop flows
summary: Hold: the briefing reports no automation for CyberArk machine configuration, although Microsoft documents its Dataverse application record and configuration fields. Its billing gap also overlooks published desktop-flow run meters, and it describes an undocumented Delinea retrieval identity and assumes the machine credentials are privileged.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because Microsoft has not published a licence specific to this provider.
claims.quote: The Power Automate Premium license provides access to all RPA premium features, except unattended RPA and hosted RPA.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and name the existing product entitlement: 'Power Automate Premium includes premium RPA features, including retrieving and using desktop-flow credentials; unattended executions require Power Automate Process. Pay-as-you-go also provides access to most premium features in its enabled environment. Microsoft has not published licensing specific to the Delinea provider.' claims.claim: CyberArk application configuration is reached in Power Automate through Machines > machine or group > Configure CyberArk.
claims.quote: From the left navigation, select Machines, and then select the machine or the group. ... In the Machine details, select Configure CyberArk. ... Select New application.
claims.fix: Expand controls[1].ui.path and the rendered path to 'Machines > machine or group > Machine details > Configure CyberArk > New application'. The present path reaches the correct configuration area but omits its heading and stops before creating the application.

claims.claim: Automation for configuring a CyberArk application on a machine or group is not documented.
claims.quote: applicationid: Unique ID of the application as registered in the CyberArk CCP. primarycertificatefile: Certificate that will be used as an SSL client certificate to contact the CCP. This field is encrypted with the group public key.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api null with kind rest, call 'POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/flowcredentialapplications', docs https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/flowcredentialapplication. Add to its note: 'Creates the CyberArk application record; applicationid names the CCP application, flowmachinegroupid associates its machine group, and primarycertificatefile carries the SSL client certificate encrypted with the group public key.' Retain the statement that this is not a Delinea setup contract.

claims.claim: Existing credentials are shared in Power Automate through Credentials > credential > Share.
claims.quote: Sign-in to Power Automate, and then go to Credentials. ... Select your credential from the list of credentials. ... On the command bar, select Share.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: The credential table supports the GrantAccess, ModifyAccess and RevokeAccess actions for access management.
claims.quote: The following operations can be used with the credential entity type. ... GrantAccess | Not Bound ... ModifyAccess | Not Bound ... RevokeAccess | Not Bound
claims.fix: Replace the descriptive action list with one explicit operation: 'POST [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/GrantAccess'. Set docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/reference/grantaccess and add to the note: 'Target identifies the credential record; PrincipalAccess identifies the recipient and access rights.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/use-web-api-actions for the unbound POST syntax. Keep ModifyAccess and RevokeAccess only as names in the prose, not as a substitute for a call.

claims.fix: Replace with: 'No separate Delinea-provider meter is published. Microsoft's Power Automate flow-run meters are in preview: in a pay-as-you-go environment, attended desktop runs cost $0.60 per run unless the user's licence includes attended RPA, and unattended runs cost $3.00 per run regardless of assigned environment capacity; these charges bill the linked Azure subscription.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pay-as-you-go-meters. Do not extend the absence of a provider-specific rate to the desktop runs themselves.
